title: Quarter-Wave Initialized 24-Layer Stack with Gradient Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness (HfO2 ~100-110 nm, SiO2 ~125-135 nm at 450 nm center) rather than uniform 200 nm will reduce boundary collisions during optimization, increasing valid_candidates while maintaining or improving best_target_score above 0.53.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory predicts maximum reflectance for minimum layer count when optical thickness equals lambda/4. For dual-band operation (UV reflection, SWIR transmission), non-quarter-wave deviations are necessary but quarter-wave initialization provides a physically meaningful starting point closer to optimal solutions.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) repeated 12 times | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite coating layers: 24. Outermost layer is SiO2 for environmental durability.
design_variables: thickness bounds 80-200 nm for HfO2, 100-180 nm for SiO2
manufacturing_considerations: outermost SiO2 layer >= 100 nm for durability
thickness bounds reflect realistic deposition control
theory_basis: Dual-band filter requires non-quarter-wave optimization from quarter-wave seed
expected_advantages: Higher valid_candidates due to reduced boundary collisions
Faster convergence from physically meaningful initialization
known_risks: Quarter-wave initialization may trap optimizer in local optimum
Dual-band conflict may still limit best_target_score below 0.7
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate. Stack sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica (12 bilayers, 24 finite layers total). Initialize HfO2 layers at 105 nm and SiO2 layers at 130 nm (quarter-wave at 450 nm center). Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds: HfO2 80-200 nm, SiO2 100-180 nm. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence across 300-450 nm (reflectance target) and 1000-1700 nm (transmittance target). Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band and mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band simultaneously. Outermost layer must be SiO2. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Restructured thickness initialization from uniform 200 nm to quarter-wave values (HfO2 105 nm, SiO2 130 nm) based on feedback directive to reduce boundary collisions. Maintains 24-layer topology from route_01 but changes seed distribution to concentrate near hypothesized resonance window.
